summary:
The United Kingdom's Equality Act 2010 and its 2025 code of practice on single-sex services do not automatically extend to Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha. Local law governs the territory, and those United Kingdom measures can apply only by Order in Council.

Consensual same-sex activity has been lawful in the territory since 2001, and the age of consent is equalised at 16 across Saint Helena, Ascension Island and Tristan da Cunha.

The 2009 constitutional order imposed by the United Kingdom bans discrimination on grounds including sexual orientation territory-wide, and those protections have been in force since 2009.

Same-sex marriage was legislated island by island. The Ascension Island Council approved the marriage ordinance on 31 May 2016 by 5 votes to 0; it was signed and gazetted on 20 June 2016 and commenced on 1 January 2017. Tristan da Cunha followed on 4 August 2017 and Saint Helena on 20 December 2017.

Adoption by same-sex couples has been permitted since 2017.

The territory is classified as an Overseas Country or Territory of the European Union, with applicability of the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights recorded on that basis.
tangentialFactors:
Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha is a British Overseas Territory, so the constitutional and legislative framework is set locally under an order made by the United Kingdom, and United Kingdom statutes reach the islands only where extended by order.

The territory's decriminalisation in 2001 and equalisation of the age of consent at 16 place it among the jurisdictions where same-sex relations were legalised comparatively late, but its non-discrimination and marriage provisions now run through local island-by-island legislation rather than United Kingdom statute.

The marriage reform proceeded through the Ascension Island Council rather than a territory-wide instrument, so each island group carries its own commencement date: Ascension Island from 1 January 2017, Tristan da Cunha from 4 August 2017, and Saint Helena from 20 December 2017.
localsOnly:
Residents of all three island groups are covered by the 2009 constitutional ban on discrimination, which includes sexual orientation as a protected ground.

Residents may marry, and adopt, regardless of the sex of a partner, under ordinances enacted locally from 2016 onward and in force from 2017.

The Ascension Island Council records its legislative votes; the 2016 marriage ordinance was carried unanimously, 5 votes to 0.
outOfScopeNotes:
Unresolved: whether EU Charter of Fundamental Rights applicability has survived the United Kingdom's departure from the European Union. The Overseas Country or Territory classification cited here comes from a source accessed in June 2013 and is not confirmed as current.

Not sourced: any provision specific to trans people on legal gender recognition, gender markers on identity documents, or access to gender-affirming healthcare in Saint Helena, Ascension or Tristan da Cunha, either in local ordinances or in any United Kingdom measure extended to the territory.

Not sourced: enforcement or complaint records under the 2009 non-discrimination protections, and whether the 2025 United Kingdom single-sex-services code has been extended to the territory by Order in Council.
